newsitem.title: USA: Officials seek recount in Dem race for Studds seat.
newsitem.headline: Officials seek recount in Dem race for Studds seat.

text.p: Massachusetts elections officials were recounting the ballots in the Democratic primary to succeed 12-term congressman Rep. Gerry Studds.

In what looked like an upset, Philip Johnston, a former state representative and regional head of U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, was leading Norfolk County District Attorney William Delahunt by about 200 votes.
Delahunt, who stressed his record as an effective prosecutor, had been favored by the polls. Johnston had staked out turf as the expert on health care reform.

Meanwhile on the Republican side, House Minority Leader Edward Teague, easily defeated his opponents Francis Sargent, Jr., son of former Republican Gov. Francis Sargent adn Steven Pappas, a newspaper deliverer.
Teague, a conservative who stressed his ability to work ina bipartisan manner, easily won the nomination with more than 60 percent of the vote.
Studds, who has served in the House for 24 years, announced he would not seek a 13th term last October.
Voter turnout was extremely light with about 15 percent of eligible voters going to the polls. Election officials blamed bad weather and few legislative contests.
